activity.notes: Miguel Hidalgo y Costilla was appointed Generalissimo of the insurgent armies of America at Acambaro on 22 October 1810 and remained the movement's principal political-military leader until he was deposed from command at Saltillo on 6 March 1811. ATLAS uses the existing Mexico polity as Hidalgo's representative own-side political community rather than New Spain or the Spanish Monarchy. This is consistent with Hidalgo's explicitly independence-oriented movement and with the first insurgent government he established at Guadalajara, which Mexican official historical institutions describe as a governmental project for a new independent nation.

sources.title: Cronología de la Independencia — 1810 — INEHRM
sources.citation_text: INEHRM records that on 22 October 1810 the Ejército Insurgente was constituted at Acámbaro and Hidalgo was appointed generalísimo de los ejércitos de América.

sources.title: Natalicio de Miguel Hidalgo — Fomento Cívico, SEGOB
sources.citation_text: Mexico's Secretaría de Gobernación records that Hidalgo was deposed from command of the insurgent movement at Saltillo on 6 March 1811, when command passed to Ignacio Allende as Generalísimo.

sources.title: Hidalgo Constituyente — INEHRM
sources.citation_text: INEHRM documents Hidalgo's plan for government, his political authority within the insurgency, and the constitutional project that developed from the independence movement toward a Mexican nation.
